key_insight: HEPTv2 is an end-to-end point-transformer that reconstructs charged-particle tracks directly from detector hits, avoiding graph construction while improving both accuracy and runtime efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The approach is highly relevant for real-time high-energy-physics systems because it delivers strong tracking performance at HL-LHC scale under tight latency and memory constraints.
method: Locality-aware point encoder using locality-sensitive hashing in detector coordinate space
Sectorized track decoder with direct hit-to-track prediction
Joint encoder-decoder supervision for end-to-end optimization without graph-building, clustering, or filtering
evidence_signal: On TrackML, HEPTv2 reports 98.6% double-majority tracking efficiency at a 0.8% fake rate, with about 15 ms inference time and 0.4 GB peak memory per event on an NVIDIA A100.
watch_item: Performance depends on efficient sectorization and hashing design, so deployment may require careful tuning to preserve accuracy at very high hit multiplicities.
paper_title: HEPTv2: End-to-End Efficient Point Transformer for Charged Particle Reconstruction
